lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Make the code link’s destination recognizable and clickable in the PDF.
items.because: The displayed path looks generic.

items.says: Confirm that the email address is professional.
Confirm that the phone number has the appropriate country code for international applications.
Remove the date of birth and nationality for US and Canadian applications.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary, consume space, and can expose you to unconscious bias.

items.says: Standardize date formatting and use proper date-range dashes instead of spaced hyphens.
Make the expected graduation status visually unambiguous.
Consider adding a strong GPA if it helps your candidacy.
Consider adding a relevant graduate focus if the degree title does not make it clear.
Name the country explicitly on the real résumé if the institution may be unfamiliar to US recruiters.
Consider a brief industry descriptor if the company is not well known.
items.because: It may help readers identify the company without making the heading cumbersome.

items.says: Verify that the October-to-May timeline matches the internship’s formal classification.
Define what “diagnostic accuracy” measures.
items.because: It could mean case-level accuracy, top-1 classification, fault localization, or another metric.

items.says: State the evaluation basis if disclosure is allowed.
items.because: The number of cases or held-out test set would give the result context.

items.says: Clarify whether 35% is a relative or percentage-point increase.
items.because: The current wording can materially overstate the result.

items.says: Explain your individual contribution to fine-tuning.
items.because: It may have been part of a larger team effort.

items.says: Consider whether the target audience will understand “validated tool-use trajectories.”
items.because: Retain the technical term only if it is central to the role.

items.says: Clarify what “in-scope signals” means and how the routing layer enforced the boundaries.
Explain why less reviewer disagreement indicates better performance.
items.because: The figure might otherwise show merely greater agreement.

items.says: Identify the evaluation size or time window behind the 14% and 6% figures.
Clarify whether you implemented the routing layer or only designed it.
Trim secondary implementation detail if the bullet is hard to read.
items.because: It contains several concepts.

items.says: Define GRPO at least once for broader software or ML audiences.
Give the number of grouped rollouts, cases, or evaluation runs if possible.
State whether the 18% and 5% reductions are relative.
Support “equal accuracy” with a test set or tolerance.
items.because: Otherwise it can sound asserted rather than measured.

items.says: Use US spelling instead of “penalises” for US applications.
items.because: The résumé should follow one spelling convention.

items.says: Simplify the terminology and emphasize the operational result if agent reinforcement learning is not central to the target roles.
Clarify whether you built the evaluation harness from scratch or extended one.
Define the scope of “citation quality.”
items.because: It could refer to correctness, completeness, entailment, or formatting.

items.says: Add the number of evaluation cases if it strengthens the claim.
Explain how the regressions were caught and what release risk they prevented.
Remove or merge the second loss-masking bullet.
items.because: It repeats the same technique as the first fine-tuning bullet without a separate outcome.

items.says: Verify and clarify the claim that loss masking taught the model to reproduce tool outputs.
items.because: Assistant-only loss masking excludes non-assistant tokens, so the claim may be inconsistent if tool outputs were in a separate tool-role channel.

items.says: Establish whether your branch caused the 68% backlog reduction.
items.because: Simultaneous process changes may also have contributed.

items.says: Include the baseline number of pending cases if available.
items.because: A percentage alone can hide scale.

items.says: Clarify what the 800+ sensor signals represent.
items.because: They might be raw inputs, derived features, or signals screened after feature extraction.

items.says: Consider moving this bullet higher.
items.because: It combines scale, launch ownership, and business impact.

items.says: Replace “by 4x” with an unambiguous memory-reduction measurement.
items.because: The current framing is ambiguous.

items.says: Specify whether memory was measured per model, GPU, or training run.
State what the memory reduction enabled.
items.because: Examples include larger batches, lower hardware requirements, or faster experimentation.

items.says: Verify whether the change was BF16 mixed precision or simply BF16 training.
items.because: The description should be technically accurate.

items.says: Add the test load or request volume.
items.because: The latency result needs context.

items.says: Clarify the cache’s correctness or invalidation strategy.
items.because: Caching could have affected data freshness.

items.says: Say whether batching and caching were measured separately or together.
Fix the mismatch between “Maintained” and “adds.”
items.because: A completed role should use consistent past tense.

items.says: Give the release-cycle duration before it became three days.
Specify the types of automated regression checks.
items.because: Model quality, latency, memory, or compatibility checks may be meaningful.

items.says: Clarify whether you operated or materially improved the pipeline.
items.because: “Maintained” can undersell ownership.

items.says: Establish that three days describes a repeatable release cycle.
items.because: It should not describe just one release.

items.says: Clarify your role in the architecture, implementation, planning, and rollout.
Add measured evidence that retries and dead-letter handling improved reliability, if available.
Verify that removing the backlog was sustained over a defined period.
items.because: “Removing” is an absolute claim.

items.says: Fix the awkward PDF line break in “dead-letter.”
items.because: Forced hyphenation can look like a typo.

items.says: Clarify what “Owner” means.
items.because: It does not show whether you created, led, maintained, or operated the project.

items.says: Add a repository link if the work is public.
Name principal runtime or framework technologies.
items.because: The technology list currently gives only the language and broad domain.

items.says: Confirm that the August 2025 start date is accurate for the application date.
items.because: It should not be future-dated.

items.says: Replace the vague “AI-first engineering practices” bullet with concrete work.
items.because: It gives no specific implementation, metric, or scope.

items.says: Substantiate “accelerating delivery” and “improving outcomes.”
items.because: Those claims have no verifiable result.

items.says: Avoid “AI-first” unless it has a precise meaning in the project.
Define the baseline for “raw conversation grew 100x.”
items.because: The comparison does not say what it is relative to.

items.says: Explain token-count measurement and what the 10K limit includes.
items.because: System instructions, tool results, and retrieved context may affect the count.

items.says: Explain why 100 turns is representative or useful.
Add a quality-retention result if task performance after compaction was measured.
Explain how elimination of deadlocks and lost results was verified.
items.because: Test duration or run count would support the claim.

items.says: Define what “50-way fan-out” counts.
items.because: It could mean agents, tool calls, tasks, or streams.

items.says: Say whether the issue occurred in production, stress tests, or both.
Qualify the absolute claim that the failures were removed unless it was validated over a meaningful period.
Clarify what kind of contributor you were.
items.because: “Contributor” does not distinguish code, research, or maintenance work.

items.says: Include a repository or publication link if public.
Add the main implementation language or framework if useful.
items.because: It may help with keyword matching.

items.says: Name a few important citation and faithfulness metrics.
items.because: Recognizable or technically meaningful names would be more informative.

items.says: Say whether the contribution was merged, released, or used by others.
Clarify whether you implemented metrics, integrated libraries, or designed the interface.
Add test coverage or evaluation scale if available.
Verify that all eight metrics were meaningfully integrated and validated.
items.because: The number eight should reflect substantive work.

items.says: Specify the Kendall statistic and the two correlated rankings or variables.
Explain “injected degradation” at a high level.
items.because: The phrase is less clear to general recruiters.

items.says: Clarify how the 0.89 correlation relates to the 400 trials.
items.because: It might have been computed across trials, degradation levels, or report rankings.

items.says: Give significance or a confidence interval if presenting a research-grade result.
Delete the backlog bullet from the research-agent project.
items.because: It duplicates the internship’s diagnostics-triage result and is unrelated to this framework, suggesting a copy-and-paste error.

items.says: Move Git out of “Programming.”
items.because: Git is a version-control tool, not a programming language.

items.says: Separate languages from tools and infrastructure.
Reflect the API, event-queue, CI, and caching experience in the skills section.
items.because: Those areas appear in the experience bullets but not in skills.

items.says: Make “agent evaluation” more specific.
items.because: The current term is broad relative to the evaluation work described.

items.says: Include relevant multi-agent and tool-use concepts.
items.because: They are demonstrated in the experience section and may be useful target keywords.

items.says: Consider adding evidenced model-evaluation, fine-tuning, and inference skills.
Use past tense consistently for completed roles and projects.
items.because: Present tense should be reserved for ongoing work.

items.says: Prevent awkward wrapping of compounds such as “tool-use.”
Ensure bullets fit cleanly in the PDF without manual line breaks.
Put the most impressive outcome-driven bullet first within each role.
